newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony unit plans PlayStation output in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Sony unit plans PlayStation output in Mexico.

text.p: Sony Computer Entertainment Inc, a unit of Sony Corp, said on Monday that it planned to start producing PlayStation game players in Mexico from the middle of this year.
The company plans to produce about 100,000 units a month, a Sony Computer spokesman said.
Currently, the company produces 32-bit PlayStation machines only in Japan and sells them on the Japanese and overseas markets, he said.
"We are planning to start producing PlayStations at Sony's new plant at Tijuana, Mexico, this summer," the Sony Computer spokesman said.
"The production pace there will be about 100,000 units a month and plant's output will be shipped to the U.S. market," he said.
Parent Sony already makes television sets and other products in Tijuana, the Sony Computer spokesman said.

A Sony spokesman said the new Tijuana plant would start operations in April and to begin with would mainly produce video recorders. It would start producing PlayStation machines in the summer, he said, without elaborating.

"Demand for PlayStations is robust around the world and supply is barely keeping up. We are currently forming production plans for PlayStations in 1997 and the start of production in Mexico will be part of the plans," the Sony Computer spokesman said.
Sony Computer stopped output of the 32-bit game console at its San Diego plant last year.
The company said in October that the decision to halt U.S. production was aimed at achieving greater economies of scale by concentrating manufacturing in Japan.
